{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-al-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"3f784fe6433efc2e5ae15a72ba4463012b6370fbe9c9128c876ae5e06006bd00","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-al-class-d:lineage:32","source_registry_sha256":"ea8231e949706ecda9f2a398d6eaf9ab30e224ac7defb0e6291b764b84ed0d95","source_liveness_sha256":"e524456f547beacfeca0647b02ef401523e58aa5b835501e7cbdd821b6546315"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Regulatory and warning signs","heading":"C — Sign types, regulatory signs and warning signs","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Sign types, regulatory signs and warning signs

FACT_ID: sec08-F01 | anchor: A43
Every driver must know signs, signals and road markings well enough to recognize them instantly and to obey regulatory signs without hesitating. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec08-F02 | anchor: A43
Signs now use more symbols and pictures because they can be recognized faster at higher speeds and from farther away. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec08-F03 | anchor: A43
A sign's shape and its color are both coded to the kind of message it carries, so learn shapes and colors as well as individual signs. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec08-F04 | anchor: A43
Traffic signs fall into three types by function: regulatory, warning, and information or guide signs. [A43]
Source: [A43 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec08-F05 | anchor: A44
Regulatory signs control how traffic moves, are black and white unless shown in their actual color, and must be obeyed. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-F06 | anchor: A44
At a 4-way stop, vehicles leave in the order they arrived, so the first one to come to a complete stop is the first one allowed to go. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-F07 | anchor: A44
When two or more vehicles reach a 4-way stop at the same moment, the one farthest to the right goes first. [A44]
Why it matters: the tie-break is position, not size of vehicle or which road looks busier.
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-F08 | anchor: A44
Even when it is your turn at a 4-way stop, wait at least a few seconds to be sure no one else starts into the intersection, because many drivers ignore the rule. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-F09 | anchor: A44
A YIELD sign tells you to slow down so you can give the right of way to pedestrians crossing and to vehicles on the intersecting road. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-F10 | anchor: A44
A white-on-red regulatory sign warns that you are heading onto a one-way highway or ramp from the wrong direction. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-F11 | anchor: A44
Another regulatory sign marks a one-way roadway whose traffic is coming toward you, and you may not enter it at that point. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-F12 | anchor: A44
The railroad regulatory sign means approach with caution and make sure every track is clear before you cross. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-F13 | anchor: A44
A no-left-turn sign means you may not turn left at that intersection. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec08-F14 | anchor: A45
Under a no-parking sign you may not park in the area even if you remain inside the car. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-F15 | anchor: A45
You may not park in a space reserved for the physically handicapped, on public or private property, unless a handicapped person drives or directs the vehicle and it visibly shows the handicapped sticker. [A45]
Why it matters: both conditions are required; the sticker alone or the person alone is not enough.
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-F16 | anchor: A45
An EMERGENCY STOPPING ONLY sign allows stopping only for real emergencies. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-F17 | anchor: A45
A LEFT LANE MUST TURN LEFT sign means traffic in the left lane has to turn left at the intersection ahead. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-F18 | anchor: A45
A NO TURNS sign means you may turn neither right nor left at that intersection. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-F19 | anchor: A45
A posted speed limit is the speed allowed under normal conditions, and a sign reading SPEED LIMIT 30 means 30 miles an hour is the top speed in that area. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-F20 | anchor: A45
Some signs post both a maximum and a minimum speed for a stretch of highway, and minimum limits usually appear on freeways and other controlled-access highways. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec08-F21 | anchor: A46
A school-zone speed limit applies during the hours the sign shows, and it may also be displayed on a lighted sign with flashing amber lights. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-F22 | anchor: A46
One regulatory sign marks where a no-passing zone begins. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-F23 | anchor: A46
Where a NO TURN ON RED sign is posted at a signal-controlled intersection, you may not turn right or left on a red light. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-F24 | anchor: A46
One regulatory sign tells you not to drive to the left of it. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-F25 | anchor: A46
A lane-use sign can require the right lane to turn right while the lane beside it may either turn right or go straight. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-F26 | anchor: A46
Double right turns are allowed only at intersections signed for them; at unsigned intersections the normal right-turn rules apply. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-F27 | anchor: A46
A one-way arrow sign means you may travel only in the direction the arrow points. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-F28 | anchor: A46
Warning signs are black on yellow, except construction-area warning signs, which are black on orange, and they warn of hazards that call for extra caution. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-F29 | anchor: A46
Fluorescent yellow on a sign marks pedestrian crossings and school zones. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-F30 | anchor: A46
Most warning signs are diamond shaped, though there are some exceptions. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec08-F31 | anchor: A47
Curve warning signs tell you of a sharp left turn, a curve to the right, a gradual curve right then left, or a winding road ahead. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-F32 | anchor: A47
Side-road warning signs show that a side road joins the highway ahead, either from the right or at an angle. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-F33 | anchor: A47
A BUMP sign warns of a bump ahead and tells you to slow down. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-F34 | anchor: A47
One warning sign means the road does not continue straight, so you must turn right or left. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-F35 | anchor: A47
A SOFT SHOULDER sign warns that the roadside is soft, so stay on the pavement. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0047]

Glossary: regulatory sign — a sign that controls traffic and must be obeyed [A44]. Warning sign — a sign, usually a diamond, that alerts you to a hazard ahead [A46]. Guide sign — the third sign type, giving information or directions [A43].
Memory aid: first to stop, first to go; a tie goes to the right [A44].
